comments.body:
Hi,
If I tweak the RdfStreamProvider in fcrepo-http-commons and add the 

 "*/*"

to the @Produces path, I'll get a 406 returned, which I think is the behavior we want. It seems counter intuitive, but functions. Is that an acceptable fix for this error? (I think a second part of this fix is to update the REST API docs to include 406 under the GET Status section).

A. Soroka - since you originally wrote this code, what do you think?

output with changed code:
-------
$bseeger>curl -H "Accept:application/turtle" -v -XGET http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/peanut

  • Hostname was NOT found in DNS cache
  • Trying ::1...
  • Connected to localhost (::1) port 8080 (#0)
    > GET /fcrepo/rest/peanut HTTP/1.1
    > User-Agent: curl/7.37.1
    > Host: localhost:8080
    > Accept:application/turtle
    >
    < HTTP/1.1 406 Not Acceptable
    > ....

-Bethany

406 is the correct code, but I have no idea why that works, and frankly, I don't like relying on what may be an implementation quirk.

Can you find out why that works?

Yeah, I feel the same way.

I'll dig deeper and see what's going on.

That is not the way to resolve this ticket, IMO.

The reason this works is due to the fact that 406 errors are generated upon trying to look up a suitable RDF writer from the supplied Accept header. If none exists, the 406 is thrown, which basically overrides what JAX-RS is already designed to handle by implementing this ourselves (a bad design, IMO): http://git.io/vEZuu

The same thing can be achieved by removing the */* attribute to the FedoraLDP class: http://git.io/vEZBF

That behavior makes much more sense in my opinion. It does have the drawback that you can't send an Accept header for Binary resources (I'm not sure what an Accept header would mean for Binary resources, though).
Fine with me.

Okay. Thanks. I remember talking about this with you Aaron and I have experimented with that some.

I wasn't sure that it was okay to make it so you can't have an Accept header for Binary resources. Sounds like it's probably fine though.

Would it make sense to add some common binary file types to that @Produces list for images? jpeg, tiff, png? I know we can't list them all, but it might be nice for basic requests like this to still succeed: 

curl -H "Accept:image/jpeg" -XGET http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/peanut/butter/goat
HTTP 406 Not Acceptable

I know the user could simply remove the Accept and it will function. Maybe most don't use the Accept header and it's a moot point.
If we're looking at the describe method, why would binary resources be coming through that method? That's for RDF.
Good point. That's me being new to Fedora and learning the system as I go.
Don't worry. By the time you learn it you'll be responsible for changing it.

Incidentally, what does this produce with your code (assuming that is a path to some sort of image)?

curl -H "Accept: application/n-triples" -XGET http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/peanut/butter/goat

I suspect you'll retrieve the full resource with a 200 status code.
Yes, I do get the full resource with a 200 status code. Not quite sure what to make of that...

Based on output it looks like all requests are going through that FedoraLdp describe() function. So, I can retrieve a binary resource that way, for better or for worse.

Just created a pull request for this:

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/966
Here's the PR: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/966

Would it make the following scenario:

curl -H "Accept: application/n-triples" -XGET http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/peanut/butter/goat

..more consistent if we additionally compared the Accept header with the stored mimeType somewhere after:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-http-api/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/http/api/ContentExposingResource.java#L170

The headers are available with the injected value of headers:

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-http-commons/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/http/commons/AbstractResource.java#L58

Not sure. Could definitely do that, but it seems like it might defeat the purpose of using the JAX-RS stuff in the first place, to have another check after the @Producers() check. I think it could get confusing and make the code much too strict if we do this. Would there be much content negotiation on a binary, anyways? (Should there even be?)

I do wonder what peoples' use cases for this might be, if there are any.
Updated my pull request. It does more mime-type checking and if it can't return the requested format (for binary or triples), the user will get a 406.
The solution to this issue should likely be rethought with an eye towards leveraging native jaxrs machinery.
